mainTopic: The פסוק of פגול: which wrong intents disqualify a קרבן, which brings כרת, and proof that פגול comes from intent at the time of offering
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא that reads the פסוק of פגול (ויקרא 7:18) word by word. It teaches that the wrong intent must not be mixed with other wrong intents. It also teaches that 'פגול' covers intent חוץ למקומו, that half-measures of the time intent and the place intent join together, and that only חוץ לזמנו brings כרת, learned from נותר. רב פפא then asks רבא what the second 'third day' פסוק in פרשת קדושים teaches. רבא answers that it limits 'outside its place' to a place that is outside for blood, meat and אימורין. רב מתנה explains why the first פסוק alone would have included every place. A new ברייתא follows: רבי אליעזר proves the פסוק is about intent at the time of offering, not actual eating on the third day. רבי עקיבא challenges him, and the ברייתא brings support from 'המקריב אותו' and from אחרים ('לא יחשב'). בן עזאי reads 'אותו' as excluding someone who is late with his vow. The גמרא then asks where בן עזאי learns that the פסוק is about the קרבן, and challenges his late-vow teaching from a ברייתא of אחרים about a בכור, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No mixing other wrong intents
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes an earlier teaching: for a קרבן to become פגול, the כהן must not mix other wrong intents into his intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He must not mix other wrong intentions into it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a teaching that started before this section. A word earlier in the פסוק teaches that פגול happens only when the wrong intent is 'clean', with no other wrong intents mixed in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the כהן has more than one kind of wrong intent at once. Then the קרבן is still פסול, but it does not get the special status of פגול. The rule depends on the intent being 'pure' פגול-intent.

keyTerms.meaning: he should not mix in
other (wrong) intentions
a קרבן made disgusting and invalid by wrong intent; eating it brings כרת

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say a mixed intent leaves the קרבן kosher. It is still פסול. It just is not פגול.

phrases.english: He should not mix into it
other intentions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's word-by-word reading of the פסוק that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פגול happens only when the כהן does not mix in other wrong intents.

steps.title: The word 'פגול' means intent outside its place
steps.stepSummary: The word 'פגול' in the פסוק teaches about intent to eat the קרבן חוץ למקומו.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'פגול': this refers to intent to eat it outside its proper place.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next word in the פסוק, 'פגול'. It says this word is talking about intent to eat the קרבן outside its set area (חוץ למקומו).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself mentions eating on 'the third day', which is a time problem. The ברייתא reads the extra word 'פגול' as adding a second kind of wrong intent, the place problem. So the פסוק now covers both time and place.

keyTerms.meaning: outside its proper place (the area where it may be eaten)

phrases.english: "Piggul":
phrases.notes: A word from the פסוק, ויקרא 7:18.

phrases.english: this is outside its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next word in the same word-by-word reading of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'פגול' covers intent to eat the קרבן חוץ למקומו.

steps.title: Half-measures of time and place join together
steps.stepSummary: The word 'יהיה' teaches that wrong intents about time and about place combine to make the needed amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It shall be' teaches that they combine with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads the next word, 'יהיה' ('it shall be'). It learns that the two kinds of wrong intent (time and place) can join together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Disqualifying a קרבן needs intent to eat a full כזית. Suppose the כהן intends half a כזית חוץ לזמנו and half a כזית חוץ למקומו. The singular word 'יהיה' treats them as one thing, so the two halves add up to a full measure and the קרבן is disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: 'it shall be' (singular)
they join together / combine

phrases.english: "It shall be":
phrases.notes: The word is singular, not 'they shall be'. That is why the two intents are treated as one.

phrases.english: teaches that they combine
this one with that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 2: now that the פסוק covers both time and place, 'יהיה' says they combine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intent of חוץ לזמנו and intent of חוץ למקומו combine to make the minimum measure for פסול.

steps.title: Only one of the two intents brings כרת
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'והנפש האוכלת ממנו' teaches that only one of the two kinds of wrong intent carries the punishment of כרת, not both.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the soul that eats of it': one, and not two.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads the end of the פסוק. The word 'ממנו' ('of it') shows that only one of the two wrong intents makes eating the קרבן a sin punished with כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both intents make the קרבן פסול, and they even combine (step 3). But the כרת punishment for eating it is limited to just one of them. 'Of it' is read as narrowing the rule to a single case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and the soul that eats of it'
one and not two
spiritual cutting off, the punishment hinted at by 'shall bear his iniquity'

phrases.english: "And the soul that eats of it":
phrases.notes: The פסוק goes on 'shall bear his iniquity', which means כרת. The word 'of it' is what limits it to one.

phrases.english: one and not two;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing the two intents combine for פסול, the ברייתא limits כרת to only one of them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one of the two wrong intents carries כרת.

steps.title: Which one brings כרת?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks which of the two intents, time or place, is the one that brings כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which one is it?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The ברייתא asks which of the two intents is the one with כרת, and gets ready to answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said 'one, not two' but did not say which one. This question asks for that missing piece.

keyTerms.meaning: and which one?

phrases.english: And which is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the detail left open by step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which intent, חוץ לזמנו or חוץ למקומו, carries כרת.

steps.title: It is intent beyond its time, learned from נותר
steps.stepSummary: The one with כרת is חוץ לזמנו. This is learned by a גזירה שוה of 'עון' and 'עון' from נותר, which is similar to חוץ לזמנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is beyond its time. We learn 'iniquity' from 'iniquity' in נותר, because נותר is similar to it in ז״ב.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: the intent that brings כרת is חוץ לזמנו, eating it after its proper time. The proof comes from comparing the word 'עון' here to the word 'עון' used for נותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about נותר (leftover קרבן meat) also says 'עון', and there it means כרת. A גזירה שוה carries that meaning over to our פסוק. It is applied to חוץ לזמנו and not to חוץ למקומו because נותר resembles the time case in the features hinted at by the letters ז״ב.

keyTerms.meaning: beyond its proper time
learning a law from the same word appearing in two places
iniquity; here it signals כרת
קרבן meat left over past the time it may be eaten
a memory shortcut, letters standing for features נותר and חוץ לזמנו share

steps.whatToRemember: Both wrong intents (time and place) make a קרבן פסול and can combine. Only חוץ לזמנו brings כרת, learned from נותר through 'עון'–'עון'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the strict punishment of פגול with כרת applies only to wrong intent about time, even though place-intent also makes the קרבן פסול.

phrases.english: this is beyond its time –
for he derives "iniquity"–"iniquity" from notar,
phrases.notes: For נותר the פסוק says 'he shall bear his iniquity' (ויקרא 19:8), and that means כרת.

phrases.english: since it resembles it in zayin-beit.
phrases.notes: ז״ב are memory letters for features נותר and חוץ לזמנו have in common. The text doesn't spell them out here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חוץ לזמנו carries כרת, learned by גזירה שוה 'עון'–'עון' from נותר, which resembles it (ז״ב).

steps.title: רב פפא asks what רבא learns from the second 'third day' verse
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks רבא what he learns from the word 'שלישי' in פרשת קדושים, since according to him the first פסוק already taught the law of the wrong place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: According to you, what do you learn from the word 'third' in the section of 'You shall be holy'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks רבא a question about his approach. The 'third day' rule appears in two פסוקים, and he wants to know what the second one is for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא used the first פסוק (ויקרא ז:יח) to teach about intending to eat חוץ למקומו. The same idea appears again in ויקרא יט:ז, and the Torah does not repeat itself for nothing. So רב פפא asks what that second פסוק adds.

keyTerms.meaning: According to you, in your own opinion
The Torah section that begins 'You shall be holy' (ויקרא יט)
What do you learn from it?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
According to you, the word "third" in the section of "You shall be holy"
what do you learn from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבא's source for חוץ למקומו (step 2) and asks about the extra פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the second 'שלישי' פסוק teaches according to רבא.

steps.title: רבא: the outside place must be outside for blood, meat, and fats
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the second פסוק teaches that the 'outside place' counts only if it is outside for all three: blood, meat, and אימורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is needed to teach about a place that is outside in three ways: for the blood, for the meat, and for the sacrificial fats.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers: the second פסוק defines which 'outside place' counts for this law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every wrong place counts as 'outside its place' for this law. The intended place must be outside the proper area for the blood, for the meat, and for the fats, all three together.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for, it is used to teach
Threefold, outside in all three ways
The fats and parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: That verse is needed
for a place that is threefold
for the blood, for the meat, and for the fats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second פסוק limits the law to a place that is outside for blood, meat, and fats.

steps.title: Why not learn this from the first verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need a second פסוק at all, since the first פסוק also uses the word 'third'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let me learn it from the first verse, 'If it be at all eaten,' since the Torah also wrote that verse with the word 'third'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer. The first פסוק also says 'third', so it could teach the 'threefold place' rule too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא already reads the first פסוק as being about place. If so, its word 'third' could also hint at the 'three ways' rule. That would make the second פסוק unnecessary again.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me derive it from, why not learn it from
The first verse
The Merciful One, a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the Torah

phrases.english: Let me derive it from the first verse:
"If it be at all eaten"
since the Merciful One wrote it with the word "third"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the second פסוק is needed for the 'threefold place' rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first פסוק also says 'third', so it could teach the same rule, which leaves the second פסוק unnecessary.

steps.title: רב מתנה: without the second verse, every place would be included
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports רב מתנה's answer: from the first פסוק alone we would use פרט וכלל and include every outside place. The second פסוק limits it to the threefold place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I said this teaching before רב מתנה, and he told me: If we learned only from there, I would have said that 'third' is a specific detail and 'פגול' is a general term. The general term adds to the detail, and all other places would be included. The second verse teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the answer he heard from רב מתנה. The first פסוק alone would include too much, so the second פסוק is needed to narrow it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פסוק, the detail ('third') comes first and the general word ('פגול') comes after. By the rule of פרט וכלל, the general word then widens the law, so any outside place would count. The second פסוק comes and limits it to a place that is outside in all three ways.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling
A specific detail in a פסוק
A general term in a פסוק
The general term adds to the detail, so the law becomes wider
This teaches us (that it is not so)

steps.confusionAlert: The rule here is פרט וכלל (detail first, then general), which WIDENS the law. Do not mix it up with כלל ופרט (general first, then detail), which narrows the law.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the first פסוק teaches the law of the wrong place, and the second פסוק narrows it to a place that is outside for blood, meat, and fats.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I said this teaching before Rav Mattana;

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: אִי מֵהָתָם, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא:
phrases.english: he said to me: If we learned it from there, I would have said:
phrases.notes: 'From there' means from the first פסוק alone.

phrases.english: "third" is a detail, "פגול" is a general term;
and the general term becomes an addition to the detail,
and all other places would be included;
so the second verse teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the first פסוק alone would lead to a wider law, so the second פסוק is needed to limit it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the first פסוק by פרט וכלל, any place outside would count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a place that is outside for blood, meat, and fats counts, as the second פסוק teaches.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the verse speaks of intending to eat on the third day
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says the פסוק 'if it be at all eaten' is talking about someone who intends, at the time of the offering, to eat it on the third day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And if any of the meat of his peace offering is at all eaten.' רבי אליעזר said: Bend your ear and listen. The verse is speaking about someone who intends to eat from his offering on the third day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new ברייתא. רבי אליעזר explains that the פסוק is not about actual eating, but about a wrong intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply read, the פסוק sounds like it is about someone who actually ate on the third day. רבי אליעזר says it really speaks of someone who intended to eat then while offering the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Bend your ear to hear, listen carefully
One who has an intent or thought during the עבודה
A peace offering

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And if any of the meat of his peace offering is at all eaten"

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: כּוֹף אׇזְנְךָ לִשְׁמוֹעַ –
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said: Bend your ear to hear:
about one who intends to eat from his offering
on the third day, the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the meaning of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'third day' פסוק is about intending, during the offering, to eat on the third day.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means actually eating on the third day?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר raises the simple reading: perhaps the פסוק is about someone who actually ate the קרבן on the third day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is only about one who actually eats from his offering on the third day?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר himself raises the other possible reading, the plain meaning of the words. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'if it be eaten' sound like real eating. So רבי אליעזר asks whether the פסוק might mean exactly that, instead of only an intent.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only
One who actually eats

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only about one who actually eats from his offering
on the third day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the plain reading as an alternative to רבי אליעזר's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the פסוק could mean actual eating on the third day.

steps.title: A fit offering cannot become disqualified later
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rejects the plain reading: a קרבן that was fine for two days cannot go back and become disqualified because someone ate it on the third day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would you say that after it was fit, it should go back and become disqualified?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר himself pushes away the suggestion of step 12 and proves his reading. That's why רבי עקיבא answers him next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the קרבן 'will not be accepted', which means the whole offering is ruined. A קרבן that was fine for two days cannot be ruined after the fact just because someone ate it late. So the פסוק must be about a wrong intent at the time of the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid, fit
It would go back and become disqualified

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that פגול is created by a wrong thought during the עבודה, not by what happens later.

phrases.english: Would you say: after it is fit,
it should go back and become disqualified?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternative reading of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that the פסוק is about actually eating on the third day.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would mean a valid קרבן becomes disqualified after the fact, which makes no sense.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: Things can become disqualified looking backward
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא challenges the claim that a valid קרבן cannot later become disqualified. He brings examples from טומאה where a later event undoes an earlier status of טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: Yes, it can happen! We find that a זב, a זבה, and a woman who watches one day for one day all have a presumption of purity. But once they see another discharge, they undo it. So you too should not be surprised that even though the קרבן was made fit, it can go back and become disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא argues against רבי אליעזר's point from step 13. He says a קרבן can be fine at first and then become disqualified going backward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said a קרבן that was valid for two days cannot become disqualified by eating on the third day. רבי עקיבא answers that הלכה does have cases like this. A זב or a זבה who immersed is treated as טהור, but a new discharge that same day undoes the טהרה looking backward, so the same could be true for a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A man or woman who becomes טמא because of an unusual bodily discharge
A woman who saw blood outside her normal time and must watch for one clean day
A presumed status of being pure
They undid it, canceling what came before
It was made fit or valid

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not saying the קרבן was never valid. His point is that it really was valid at first, and a later event can cancel that looking backward.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: Yes!
We find with a zav and a zava
and a woman who watches a day for a day
that they have a presumption of purity,
but once they saw, they undid it;
phrases.notes: 'Saw' means they saw another discharge that same day, which cancels the purity going backward.

phrases.aramaic: אַף אַתָּה אַל תִּתְמַהּ עַל זֶה –
phrases.english: you too should not be surprised at this
that even though it was made fit,
it can go back and become disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: הֵן! מָצִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of the דחיה in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's claim that a valid קרבן cannot later become disqualified
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are known cases where a later event cancels an earlier valid status looking backward, so the same could happen with a קרבן.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: The word 'he who offers' points to the time of offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers from the פסוק. The word 'המקריב' shows that the disqualification happens at the time of offering, not on the third day.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But the פסוק says 'he who offers.' This shows the קרבן becomes disqualified at the time of offering, and not on the third day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends his position against רבי עקיבא. Instead of arguing from logic, he points to a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא showed that disqualifying something looking backward is possible. רבי אליעזר answers that the פסוק itself ties the disqualification to the moment of offering by saying 'המקריב'. That means the problem is the intention during the offering, not later eating.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who offers the קרבן
The time when the קרבן is offered
Becomes disqualified

phrases.english: He said to him: But it says "he who offers"
phrases.notes: 'He' here is רבי אליעזר. The word comes from the same פסוק: ויקרא 7:18.

phrases.english: at the time of offering it becomes disqualified,
and it is not disqualified on the third day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's challenge with a proof from the פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Logic alone allows a disqualification looking backward on the third day
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'המקריב' places the disqualification at the time of offering

steps.title: Maybe 'he who offers' means the priest
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks himself whether 'המקריב' might be describing the כהן who offers, rather than the time of offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps when it says 'he who offers,' it only means the priest who offers the קרבן?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר is still talking: he checks whether his own proof really works. He raises another way to read the word 'המקריב'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'המקריב' simply means the כהן, it would teach something about the person and not about when the disqualification happens. This would weaken רבי אליעזר's proof, so the next step needs to settle it.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן who performs the offering

phrases.english: Or perhaps it says "he who offers"
only to mean the priest who offers?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר ״הַמַּקְרִיב״ אֶלָּא זֶה כֹּהֵן הַמַּקְרִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the reading of 'המקריב' used in step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'המקריב' refer to the time of offering or to the כהן himself?

steps.title: The word 'it' shows the פסוק is about the offering
steps.stepSummary: Because the פסוק says 'אותו', it is talking about the קרבן and not the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'it,' the פסוק is talking about the offering, and it is not talking about the priest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers his own question from step 16. The extra word 'אותו' shows the פסוק is about the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק meant only the כהן, it could have said 'המקריב לא יחשב' without adding 'אותו'. Saying 'המקריב אותו' makes the קרבן the subject of the disqualification, so רבי אליעזר's proof holds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It', referring here to the קרבן
An animal offering

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's proof is that 'המקריב אותו' links the disqualification to the קרבן at the time it is offered, not to eating on the third day.

phrases.english: When it says "it"
it is talking about the offering,
and it is not talking about the priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'אותו' makes the קרבן the subject, so 'המקריב' is not just a description of the כהן

steps.title: בן עזאי: 'It' excludes someone who is late with his vow
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי explains the word 'אותו' differently. Only the פגול offering becomes 'not accepted.' Someone who is late in bringing his vowed offering does not lose it.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: Why does the פסוק say 'it'? Because it says 'you shall not delay paying it,' I might think that even someone who is late with his vow falls under 'it shall not be accepted.' So the פסוק says 'it': this one is 'not accepted,' but someone who is late with his vow is not under 'it shall not be accepted.'
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי gives his own explanation of what the word 'אותו' teaches. He uses it to exclude someone who delays his vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a separate לאו against delaying a vowed offering. We might have thought that breaking it also makes the קרבן 'not accepted', like פגול. 'אותו' limits 'לא ירצה' to this קרבן, so a late offering is still accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק come to teach?
'Do not delay paying it', the לאו against being late with a vow
Someone who is late in fulfilling his vow
'It shall not be accepted'
One might have thought

steps.confusionAlert: Delaying a vow is still an עבירה. בן עזאי only teaches that the delayed קרבן is not disqualified.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: ״אֹתוֹ״ מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר?
phrases.english: Ben Azzai says: "It" — what does it come to teach?
Since it is stated: "You shall not delay paying it"

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף מְאַחֵר נִדְרוֹ בְּלֹא יֵרָצֶה?
phrases.english: one might think that even one who delays his vow is under "it shall not be accepted"?
So the verse says: "It"
it is under "it shall not be accepted,"
phrases.notes: 'It' means this offering, the one with the wrong intention, which the פסוק is discussing.

phrases.english: but one who delays his vow is not under "it shall not be accepted."

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: ״אֹתוֹ״ מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different use for the word 'אותו' than the one in step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who delays his vowed offering does not have it disqualified as 'לא ירצה'.

steps.title: אחרים: 'It shall not be credited' points to intention
steps.stepSummary: אחרים learn from the word 'יחשב' that the disqualification comes from מחשבה, not from eating on the third day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: 'It shall not be credited' (יחשב) shows the offering is disqualified by intention, and it is not disqualified on the third day.
steps.whatsHappening: אחרים give another source for רבי אליעזר's view. They read 'לא יחשב' as hinting at מחשבה, a wrong intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יחשב' has the same root as 'מחשבה'. So the פסוק itself is talking about a wrong thought at the time of offering, and not about someone actually eating the קרבן on the third day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a תנא quoted without a name
'It shall not be credited'
Intention or thought

steps.whatToRemember: Two readings support the idea that פגול comes from intention at the time of offering: 'המקריב אותו' (רבי אליעזר) and 'לא יחשב' (אחרים). בן עזאי uses 'אותו' for something else: to exclude a delayed vow.

phrases.english: Others say: "It shall not be credited"
it is disqualified by intention,
phrases.notes: יחשב and מחשבה share the same Hebrew root, which is the whole proof.

phrases.english: and it is not disqualified on the third day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another source, besides 'המקריב', that the disqualification comes from intention
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disqualification of 'פגול' comes from intention, as hinted by 'יחשב', and not from eating on the third day.

steps.title: How does בן עזאי know the פסוק is about the offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where בן עזאי learns that the פסוק is talking about the קרבן and not the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בן עזאי: where does he learn that the פסוק is talking about the offering and not about the כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where בן עזאי gets the idea that the פסוק is about the קרבן, since he used the word 'אותו' for a different teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17 the ברייתא used 'אותו' to show the פסוק is about the קרבן and not the כהן. בן עזאי used 'אותו' for his own teaching about a late vow (Step 18). So he needs another source to show the פסוק is about the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal offering (קרבן)
The priest who offers the קרבן
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And בן עזאי,
that the verse is speaking about the offering
phrases.notes: This is the point the ברייתא proved from 'אותו' back in Step 17.

phrases.english: and not about the כהן,
from where does he know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for בן עזאי's source, since he used 'אותו' for his own teaching
steps.sheelahInformationSought: בן עזאי's source that the פסוק of פגול refers to the קרבן and not to the כהן

steps.title: Two answers: from אחרים, or from the word 'ירצה'
steps.stepSummary: Answer one: בן עזאי learns it from אחרים. Answer two: the words 'לא ירצו' and 'לא ירצה' only fit a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: he learns it from אחרים. Or if you want, say: since the פסוק writes 'they will not be accepted' and 'it will not be accepted', it must be about an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two possible sources for בן עזאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: אחרים learned from 'יחשב' that the problem comes from מחשבה and not from eating on the third day (Step 19). That teaching only makes sense if the פסוק is about the קרבן, so בן עזאי can rely on it. Second answer: being 'accepted' or 'not accepted' is language used for a קרבן, not for a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one possible answer)
He derives it from
It will not be accepted
An offering (Aramaic for זבח)

phrases.english: If you want, say:
he derives it from אחרים,
phrases.notes: This is the teaching of אחרים from Step 19, about the word 'יחשב'.

phrases.english: and if you want, say: from what is written, 'they will not be accepted'
and 'it will not be accepted',
it is talking about an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדַּאֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20 with two possible sources
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either from the teaching of אחרים, which assumes the פסוק is about the offering, or from the word 'ירצה', which only fits an offering

steps.title: The late-vow rule already comes from אחרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בן עזאי: his rule that a late vow is not disqualified already comes from a teaching of אחרים, so why learn it from 'אותו'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And בן עזאי said: 'it' (פגול) falls under 'it will not be accepted,' but one who is late with his vow does not. Is this learned from here? It is learned from אחרים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks בן עזאי's teaching from Step 18. That rule seems to come from somewhere else already.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי used 'אותו' to teach that a late vow is not disqualified. The גמרא says this rule is already taught by אחרים. If so, the word 'אותו' should not be needed for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who is late in bringing the קרבן he vowed
Is it learned from here?

phrases.english: And בן עזאי said:
'it' is included in 'it will not be accepted,'
phrases.notes: 'It' means the פגול offering, as בן עזאי explained in Step 18.

phrases.english: but one who is late with his vow is not included in 'it will not be accepted,'
is this learned from here?!
It is learned from אחרים!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from בן עזאי's reading of the פסוק to challenge his own teaching about a late vow
steps.kashyaTarget: בן עזאי's teaching from 'אותו' that a late vow is not disqualified
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same rule is already taught by אחרים, so 'אותו' should not be needed to teach it

steps.title: The ברייתא of אחרים about a בכור whose year passed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the ברייתא of אחרים. It talks about a בכור whose first year passed before it was brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: אחרים say: One might think that a בכור whose year has passed should be...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing the ברייתא that supports its challenge. The quote continues past this part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור should be offered within its first year. The ברייתא begins to ask whether one whose year passed is disqualified. This is the source the גמרא says already teaches that lateness does not disqualify a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, given to the כהן and brought as a קרבן
Whose first year has passed

phrases.english: As it was taught: אחרים say:
One might think that a firstborn animal
whose year has passed should be...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the challenge of Step 22
steps.raayaObject: That the rule about lateness not disqualifying a קרבן is already taught by אחרים
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of אחרים about a בכור whose first year has passed
